source_text:
φιλοσόφων περὶ ἀληθείας λέγειν ἐπαγγελλόμενα. Τοῦτο δὲ πεποιήκαμεν
μιμησάμενοί τε τὸν πρὸ ἡμῶν πολλοὺς ὠφελήσαντα Πάνταινον, οὐκ ὀλίγην ἐν
ἐκείνοις ἐσχηκότα παρασκευήν, καὶ τὸν νῦν ἐν τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καθεζόμενον
Ἀλεξανδρέων Ἡρακλᾶν, ὅντινα εὗρον παρὰ τῷ διδασκάλῳ τῶν φιλοσόφων
thought_title: Origen's examination of philosophers' truth-claims and his models
orientation: Origen is explaining why he examined both heretical doctrines and what philosophers claimed to teach about truth, and he names Pantaenus and Heraclas as his models.
pass_a_gloss: the things by the philosophers being claimed to teach about truth. And this we have done, imitating both Pantaenus, the one before us who helped many, having had no small preparation in those things, and Heraclas, the one now sitting in the presbyterate of the Alexandrians, whom I found at the teacher of philosophy

choices.why: The participle is middle/passive and modifies 'the things'; 'being announced' keeps the passive force and the sense of public claim without over-translating as 'professing'.
The glossary fixes 'presbyterate' for this term, referring to the body or office of presbyters.
The noun means readiness or training; 'preparation' fits the context of Pantaenus's considerable background in these matters.
The verb literally means 'sitting' and is used of holding an official seat; keeping the literal sense preserves the image of occupying the presbyterate.

pass_b_english: philosophers claim to teach about truth. I did this in imitation of Pantaenus, who before us helped many and had no small preparation in these matters, and also of Heraclas, who now sits in the presbyterate of Alexandria. I found Heraclas studying under the teacher of philosophy,

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'Greek learning' for Ἑλληνικῶν μαθημάτων; 'philosophical learning' not banned but 'Greek learning' is the fixed term for the educational context here.
last_rejected.fix: at the teacher of Greek learning
last_rejected.ruling: Source says τῶν φιλοσόφων ('of philosophers'), not Ἑλληνικῶν μαθημάτων; glossary rule for latter is irrelevant here.
